changes.description: A study area accepts a GeoJSON polygon file from the practitioner's own device, named by a property they name, and each feature becomes a selectable unit exactly as a downloaded administrative level does. Of the five port types only `polygons` had no source widget; the answer was not a sixth source, because a study area already held several published outlines with provenance naming each. The practitioner, 2026-10-24: "Study area then for polygon input. I have mentioned before that a study area is actually a polygon input." Provenance for a local file states "not stated" for licence, authority and year rather than inventing them, and names the file.

ADJACENT UNITS ARE ADMITTED. Parts sharing a border were refused -- two squares meeting along an edge were rejected while the same two with a gap were accepted -- so a multi-part study area worked only for units that do not touch, which administrative units tiling their ground almost never are. The practitioner, 2026-10-24: "Study area can hold adjacent units, like North Kivu and Ituri Provinces for Ebola outbreak." Two causes, both fixed: the edge test refused touching as well as crossing between parts, and the containment test probed from a vertex that for an adjacent unit usually lies on the shared border, which ray casting reads as inside. Crossing interiors and true containment are still refused, and within one part a ring that touches itself is still a drawing fault. Combined area's manual already argued this position -- two provinces sharing a border come through as two parts, not one welded outline -- so the widget kept the border while acquisition refused it; that is resolved.

Per-part identity survives into the workflow. BoundaryProvenance gains `units`, so `units[i]` names part i. A54 asks to select boundary members without forcing a union and acquisition honoured it, but application did not: several units became one MultiPolygon and one comma-joined name, so nothing could match a figure to the boundary it belongs to.

evidence.note: Repository regression coverage exists; this release entry does not certify a widget independently.
